text: You're crouched outside the bakery, tying your shoelace.
One more pull and it holds.
Friction is gone. The knot slides itself open.
Your coffee leaves the table like it's on a rink.
The taxi hits the brakes. The brakes do nothing.
It needed twelve metres to stop. It gets seventy.
Nobody can walk, either. You push, and the street just lets you go.
Mittens is having the fastest nap of her life.
Every screw, nail and knot in the city is quietly letting go.
Out there, hillsides and sand dunes would flow like water.
Then it all comes back at once.
Everything that was gliding stops exactly where it is.
Your lace pulls tight on the first try.
The strangest part? Your knees never noticed. They're smoother than ice.
